answer: Each identity has to pass a weekly liveness check in which a verifier sends a fresh puzzle that has to be solved on that agent's own attested kernel, inside a hardware enclave, within 90 seconds. One enclave key signs for exactly one ID. A farm can't let fakes wander between machines or share a solver, because the attestation binds every answer to a single chip. So each extra fake means another physical device running all the time, at about $40 a month in power and rent. That cost grows in a straight line with the number of IDs, and no bulk discount lowers it below the price of the hardware.
